title: PlayerGui
summary: Each player's LIVE GUI container: at spawn, StarterGui's contents are copied here, and this copy is what actually renders on screen. All runtime GUI changes happen here.

details.heading: Location
details.body: PlayerGui lives under each Player: `player:WaitForChild("PlayerGui")`. Client: `game.Players.LocalPlayer:WaitForChild("PlayerGui")`.

details.heading: Reset on spawn
details.body: Depending on StarterGui.ResetPlayerGuiOnSpawn and each ScreenGui.ResetOnSpawn, contents may be cleared and re-copied from StarterGui at respawn.

explanation.whatItIs: The actual screen contents for one player — the live copy of whatever was templated in StarterGui, plus anything created at runtime.
explanation.whyItExists: Every player needs independent GUI state; PlayerGui is each one's private canvas.
whenToUse: Every runtime GUI change: find the ScreenGui HERE, not in StarterGui
Checking what's on screen for a specific player
whenNotToUse: As a template store — design-time GUI belongs in StarterGui
From Scripts on the server without going through the right player object
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
StarterGui ──copy at spawn──▶ PlayerGui ──renders──▶ screen
                               ▲
                    runtime changes go HERE
```
tips: Client access: LocalPlayer:WaitForChild("PlayerGui") — it may not exist in the first instants
ScreenGui.ResetOnSpawn = false keeps a GUI across deaths
Server updating everyone's GUI: RemoteEvent → each client edits its own PlayerGui
commonMistakes: Editing StarterGui at runtime (the #1 GUI bug — see gotcha)
Forgetting WaitForChild on PlayerGui from a fast-running LocalScript
Assuming a GUI you made survives respawn without ResetOnSpawn=false

examples.title: Runtime GUI, the right way
examples.code:
-- LocalScript
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local playerGui = Players.LocalPlayer:WaitForChild("PlayerGui")

local gui = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
gui.Name = "RuntimeHUD"
gui.ResetOnSpawn = false

local label = Instance.new("TextLabel")
label.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(300, 50)
label.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0)
label.Text = "Hello from PlayerGui!"
label.Parent = gui

gui.Parent = playerGui   -- appears immediately on screen
